title_en: Wang Xinghua, Wang Zhenzhong, Lyu Wenfu, and Mei Mingyu v. Heilongjiang No.1 Radio Factory — dispute over patent implementation license contract
ruling_gist_en: Where a patentee and other non-patentee(s) jointly act as one party to a contract and enter into a patent exploitation license contract with another party, and the contract explicitly stipulates the rights and obligations of such other non-patentee(s), the patentee's exercise of patent rights shall be bound by the contract. Without the consent of such other non-patentee(s), the patentee has no right to unilaterally terminate the patent exploitation license contract.

full_text_en:
Wang Xinghua, Wang Zhenzhong, Lyu Wenfu, and Mei Mingyu v. Heilongjiang Radio Factory No. 1 — Dispute over Patent Exploitation License Contract

【Ruling Summary】

Where a patentee, together with other non-patentee persons, acts as one party to a contract and enters into a patent exploitation license contract with another party, and the contract explicitly stipulates the rights and obligations of such non-patentee persons, the patentee's exercise of patent rights shall be bound by the contract. Without the consent of such non-patentee persons, the patentee has no right to unilaterally terminate the patent exploitation license contract.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2006) Min San Ti Zi No. 2

Re-applicant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance, Original Re-respondent): Wang Xinghua, male, 68 years old, Han ethnicity, retired cadre of Heilongjiang Provincial Bureau of Technical Supervision, residing at No. 11 Yanqiang Street, Dongli District, Harbin City.

Re-applicant (Third Party at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance, Original Re-respondent): Wang Zhenzhong, male, 66 years old, Han ethnicity, former senior engineer of State-owned Fenghua Machinery Factory, now retired, residing at Building 42, Fenghua District, Dongli District, Harbin City.

Re-applicant (Third Party at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance, Original Re-respondent): Lyu Wenfu, male, 73 years old, Han ethnicity, former senior engineer of State-owned Fenghua Machinery Factory, now retired, residing at No. 16 Dier Fangyuanli, Nangang District, Harbin City.

Re-applicant (Third Party at First Instance): Mei Mingyu, male, 68 years old, Han ethnicity, former senior engineer of State-owned Fenghua Machinery Factory, now retired, residing at No. 11 Yanqiang Street, Dongli District, Harbin City.

Agent ad litem: Wang Xinghua, male, 68 years old, Han ethnicity, retired cadre of Heilongjiang Provincial Bureau of Technical Supervision, residing at No. 11 Yanqiang Street, Dongli District, Harbin City.

Re-respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance, Original Re-applicant): Heilongjiang Radio Factory No. 1, domiciled at Shengli Street, Acheng City, Heilongjiang Province.

Legal Representative: Li Yingjie, Factory Director.

Agent ad litem: Chen Senlin, Attorney at Beijing Kunlun Law Firm.

Re-applicants Wang Xinghua, Wang Zhenzhong, Lyu Wenfu, and Mei Mingyu, due to a dispute over a patent exploitation license contract, applied to this Court for retrial, dissatisfied with the Civil Judgment (2002) Hei Gao Shang Zai Zi No. 12 rendered by the Heilongjiang High People's Court. Upon review, this Court found that the application of the re-applicants met the conditions for retrial filing under Article 179, Paragraph 1, Items (3) and (4) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and on March 23, 2006, ordered a retrial of this case by Civil Ruling (2003) Min San Jian Zi No. 8-1. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel composed of Presiding Judge Wang Yongchang, Acting Judges Xia Junli and Wang Yanfang, and held a public hearing of this case. Court Clerk Bao Shuo served as court recorder. Wang Xinghua, agent ad litem for re-applicants Wang Xinghua, Wang Zhenzhong, Lyu Wenfu, and Mei Mingyu, and Chen Senlin, agent ad litem for re-respondent Heilongjiang Radio Factory No. 1 (hereinafter referred to as Radio Factory No. 1), appeared in court. This case is now concluded.

The Harbin Intermediate People's Court found at first instance: On November 1, 1990, Wang Xinghua and Radio Factory No. 1 entered into a patent exploitation license contract, which mainly stipulated: "Wang Xinghua assigns the right to use his utility model patent, the portable personal bath box (patent application number 88202076.5, patent term from March 19, 1988 to March 19, 1996), to Radio Factory No. 1 for a fee. Radio Factory No. 1 has the exclusive right to use the patent nationwide and the right to sell; Wang Xinghua shall provide the complete set of drawings and design materials for the patented product; during the term of the contract, both parties may make technical improvements to the patent due to process or other production needs, but such improvements shall not affect or alter the attributes of the patent or the execution of this contract; Radio Factory No. 1 shall pay Wang Xinghua an initial fee of RMB 12,000 (already paid RMB 13,000) on the effective date of the contract; from October 1, 1990 to October 1, 1991, Radio Factory No. 1 shall pay Wang Xinghua a patent royalty of 2.5% of sales revenue; from October 1, 1991 to March 19, 1996, Radio Factory No. 1 shall pay Wang Xinghua a royalty of 2.6% of sales revenue; royalties shall be settled monthly, with settlement and payment due by the 5th of each month for the previous month; if Radio Factory No. 1 fails to pay Wang Xinghua royalties on time, it shall pay Wang Xinghua a late penalty of 5% per month." After the contract was signed, Radio Factory No. 1 commenced production. On March 20, 1991, Wang Xinghua and Radio Factory No. 1 signed an agreement to terminate the contract, citing as the main reason that the structural form of the portable personal bath box covered by the contract could not be implemented in production. Radio Factory No. 1 sold 4,846 units of the S-400A model from October 1990 to March 20, 1991, with sales revenue of RMB 2,460,451. According to the judgment (96) Dong Jing Chu Zi No. 179 of the Dongli District People's Court, Radio Factory No. 1 had paid royalties of RMB 170,948.8 and an initial fee of RMB 25,128. Wang Zhenzhong, a third party, borrowed RMB 7,000 from Radio Factory No. 1 on two occasions in October 1991. Radio Factory No. 1 paid individual income tax of RMB 43,828.49 on behalf of the parties. It was further found that the patent ownership dispute between Wang Xinghua and the three third parties, Wang Zhenzhong, Lyu Wenfu, and Mei Mingyu, had been confirmed by the judgment (94) Ha Jing Chu Zi No. 229 of the Harbin Intermediate People's Court, which determined that the "portable personal bath box" utility model, being a non-service invention, was jointly owned by Wang Xinghua, Wang Zhenzhong, and Lyu Wenfu, with the benefit distribution ratio of 45% for Wang Xinghua, 35% for Wang Zhenzhong, 15% for Lyu Wenfu, and 5% for Mei Mingyu. That judgment had become legally effective. During the litigation of this case, Wang Xinghua raised objections to the "Termination Agreement," and upon entrustment by the court of first instance, the Ministry of Public Security conducted a technical appraisal, concluding that, apart from the signature of Zhang Shijie, Wang Xinghua's signature was written by Wang Xinghua himself.

The court of first instance held: The patent exploitation license contract between Wang Xinghua and Radio Factory No. 1 is valid. The termination agreement voluntarily signed by both parties during the performance of the contract, based on actual circumstances, does not violate the law. Since the court's judgment confirmed that the patent is jointly owned by Wang Xinghua, Wang Zhenzhong, and Lyu Wenfu, Radio Factory No. 1 shall pay the corresponding royalties to Wang Xinghua, Wang Zhenzhong, Lyu Wenfu, and Mei Mingyu as agreed, with the royalties calculated up to the date of the termination agreement. Radio Factory No. 1 had already paid these amounts in fact, and Wang Xinghua, Wang Zhenzhong, Lyu Wenfu, and Mei Mingyu shall share the amounts according to the distribution ratio confirmed by the court's judgment. Whether the production and sale of "portable personal bath boxes" by Radio Factory No. 1 after the termination agreement constituted patent infringement shall be pursued by the parties in a separate action. The claims by Wang Xinghua, Wang Zhenzhong, Lyu Wenfu, and Mei Mingyu for continued payment of royalties after the termination agreement have no legal basis. Pursuant to Article 26, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Economic Contract Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 12 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, the court dismissed the claims of plaintiff Wang Xinghua and third parties Wang Zhenzhong, Lyu Wenfu, and Mei Mingyu, and ordered them to bear the corresponding litigation costs.

After the first-instance judgment, Wang Xinghua, Wang Zhenzhong, and Lyu Wenfu appealed. Wang Xinghua appealed, arguing that he did not sign the termination agreement with Radio Factory No. 1. Wang Zhenzhong and Lyu Wenfu appealed, arguing that even if Wang Xinghua had signed the termination agreement, it should be invalid. Radio Factory No. 1 argued in defense that the termination agreement was valid.

The Heilongjiang High People's Court further found at second instance: 1. On September 1, 1989, Wang Xinghua, Wang Zhenzhong, and Mei Mingyu signed a patent technology transfer contract with Radio Factory No. 1, and on October 14, 1989, submitted the complete set of drawings and design materials to Radio Factory No. 1, which paid an initial fee of RMB 13,000 as agreed. Subsequently, debugging and trial production were carried out. Based on this contract, and at the request of Radio Factory No. 1, Wang Xinghua, Wang Zhenzhong, and Mei Mingyu signed a new exclusive patent exploitation license contract with Radio Factory No. 1. Wang Xinghua signed the contract text on behalf of Wang Zhenzhong and Mei Mingyu. 2. From October 1990 to March 1996, Radio Factory No. 1 improved the patent technology for the portable personal bath box (patent no. 88202076.5), successively producing the S-400A and S-400B model bath boxes. The S-400B model bath box was granted utility model patent no. 93211464.8 by the Chinese Patent Office on March 11, 1994. During the validity period of Wang Xinghua's patent, Radio Factory No. 1 produced a total of 291,847 units of S-400A and S-400B bath boxes and sold 270,086 units. From October 1989 to July 10, 1993, Radio Factory No. 1 paid royalties of RMB 177,948.80, an initial fee of RMB 25,128, and paid individual income tax of RMB 43,828.49 on behalf of the parties. After July 10, 1993, Radio Factory No. 1 ceased paying patent royalties.

The court of second instance held: The "exclusive patent exploitation license contract" signed on November 1, 1990, by Wang Xinghua personally and on behalf of Wang Zhenzhong and Mei Mingyu with Radio Factory No. 1, represents the true intentions of both parties, does not violate the law, and should be deemed valid. However, the provisions in Articles 10 and 11 of the contract, regarding a 5% monthly late penalty for Radio Factory No. 1's failure to pay royalties on time and a 5% compensation for economic losses in case of breach by either party, lack legal basis and should not be protected. At the time of signing the contract, Wang Xinghua signed the contract text as a representative of the three persons, which Radio Factory No. 1 was aware of. On March 20, 1991, Wang Xinghua, without obtaining the consent or authorization of Wang Zhenzhong and Mei Mingyu, signed the "Termination Agreement" with Radio Factory No. 1 in his own name, infringing upon the lawful rights and interests of others. Moreover, after the termination agreement was signed, Radio Factory No. 1 did not return the complete set of drawings and design materials of the technology and continued to use the patented technology for production, even paying patent royalties until July 10, 1993. These actions indicate that the termination agreement was not actually performed. After the ownership dispute arose among Wang Xinghua and others, the relevant authorities and courts confirmed that the patent was jointly owned by Wang Xinghua, Wang Zhenzhong, and Lyu Wenfu. According to law, as of the date of grant of the patent by the Chinese Patent Office on June 1, 1989, the patent was jointly owned by Wang Xinghua, Wang Zhenzhong, and Lyu Wenfu. Wang Xinghua's unilateral signing of the "Termination Agreement" with Radio Factory No. 1 in his own name should be deemed invalid. The first-instance court's finding that the termination agreement between Wang Xinghua and Radio Factory No. 1 was valid was improper and should be corrected. Radio Factory No. 1 shall pay patent royalties to Wang Xinghua, Wang Zhenzhong, Lyu Wenfu, and Mei Mingyu in accordance with the exclusive license contract. Given that, during the implementation of the patent, Radio Factory No. 1 made improvements to the technology, and the sales price of the bath boxes increased from approximately RMB 495 per unit to around RMB 1,000, the patent royalties should be calculated based on the original price of RMB 495 per unit. Radio Factory No. 1 sold a total of 270,086 bath boxes from November 1, 1990, to March 19, 1996, and should pay royalties of RMB 3,464,622.81, deducting the already paid amount of RMB 177,948.80 and the taxes paid on behalf of RMB 43,828.49, leaving an outstanding amount of RMB 3,242,844.52. Pursuant to Article 12 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court ruled: 1. The first-instance judgment was reversed; 2. Radio Factory No. 1 shall pay Wang Xinghua, Wang Zhenzhong, Lyu Wenfu, and Mei Mingyu patent royalties of RMB 3,242,844.52. The court acceptance fees and appraisal fees for the first and second instances, totaling RMB 46,224.22, shall be borne by Radio Factory No. 1.

Radio Factory No. 1, dissatisfied with the final judgment, argued that both the patent exploitation license contract and the termination agreement signed with Wang Xinghua were legally valid, and that Wang Zhenzhong and the other two were not the owners of the patent right under the aforementioned contracts. It further argued that the second-instance judgment seriously erred by including the S-400A product, which was unrelated to Wang Xinghua's patent, and the S-400B product, for which Radio Factory No. 1 held a patent, within the scope of the royalty payment obligation. Radio Factory No. 1 petitioned the court of second instance for retrial. On February 18, 1998, the Heilongjiang High People's Court rejected the petition by Letter (98) Hei Gao Gao Zi No. 8. In October 1998, Radio Factory No. 1 applied to this Court for retrial, and this Court referred the matter to the Heilongjiang High People's Court for review.

On March 20, 2002, the Heilongjiang High People's Court, by Civil Ruling (2001) Hei Jian Jing Jian Zi No. 81, ordered a new collegial panel to conduct a retrial of this case.

On retrial, the Heilongjiang High People's Court further found: 1. The "Termination Agreement" was drafted and signed personally by Wang Xinghua, with the signature of Zhang Shijie, the then legal representative of Radio Factory No. 1, and the affixing of the official seal. Prior to this, Wang Xinghua and Mei Mingyu had applied for a patent for a portable electric heating sauna bath box with patent number 91204101.3 to the Chinese Patent Office. The purpose of Wang Xinghua's signing of the termination agreement with Radio Factory No. 1 was to use the patent for the portable electric heating sauna bath box (no. 91204101.3) to protect the S-400A product then being produced by Radio Factory No. 1. 2. During the second-instance proceedings, the Heilongjiang High People's Court had entrusted the Intellectual Property Affairs Center of the State Science and Technology Commission to conduct a technical appraisal on whether the technical solutions of the S-400A product and the S-400B patented product produced by Radio Factory No. 1 fell within the protection scope of Wang Xinghua et al.'s portable personal bath box patent (no. 88202076.5). The appraisal conclusion stated: "The technical features of Radio Factory No. 1's Beiyan brand S-400A portable personal bath box product and the technical features of the sauna bath box patent (patent no. 93211364.8), i.e., the S-400B product, do not completely cover all essential technical features of the portable personal bath box patent (patent no. 88202076.5) and do not fall within the protection scope of that patent."

The court on retrial held: Wang Xinghua, as the sole patentee of patent no. 88202076.5 at that time, signed the patent exploitation license contract with Radio Factory No. 1. Although he signed on behalf of non-patentees Wang Zhenzhong and Mei Mingyu (excluding Lyu Wenfu), the contract did not stipulate that the right to dispose of the patent was jointly owned by the three persons, nor did it set forth any allocation of the proceeds from the patent license to Wang Zhenzhong and Mei Mingyu. On March 20, 1991, when Wang Xinghua signed the termination agreement with Radio Factory No. 1, he remained the sole patentee as recorded on the patent certificate. Radio Factory No. 1 signed the termination agreement at the request of patentee Wang Xinghua. During this period, the co-ownership rights of Wang Zhenzhong, Lyu Wenfu, and Mei Mingyu over patent no. 88202076.5 with Wang Xinghua had not yet been confirmed by law. Furthermore, the plaintiff and third parties did not provide evidence to show that Radio Factory No. 1, in signing the termination agreement at Wang Xinghua's request, acted with malice harming the lawful rights of the third parties. Both the license contract and the termination agreement were signed by Wang Xinghua alone as the licensor, so their validity should be determined consistently. The two contracts signed by Wang Xinghua in his capacity as patentee with Radio Factory No. 1 complied with the provisions of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China and are both valid. Once the patent was confirmed to be jointly owned, Radio Factory No. 1's obligations under the patent license contract had already been discharged by the termination agreement, and no contractual relationship existed between Radio Factory No. 1 and Wang Xinghua et al. The second-instance judgment's denial of the objective fact that the contract had been terminated before the confirmation of co-ownership by third parties, based on the subsequent confirmation of the patent co-ownership, lacks legal basis. The subsequently improved S-400A bath box by Radio Factory No. 1 and the S-400B bath box, which was granted a patent by the Chinese Patent Office, were appraised by the Intellectual Property Affairs Center of the State Science and Technology Commission, and their technical features did not completely cover all essential technical features of the portable personal bath box patent no. 88202076.5, and did not fall within the protection scope of that patent. Therefore, the second-instance judgment, which found that the S-400A and S-400B bath boxes produced by Radio Factory No. 1 were the patented products of Wang Xinghua et al., and ordered Radio Factory No. 1 to pay an additional patent royalty of over RMB 3.24 million to Wang Xinghua, Wang Zhenzhong, Mei Mingyu, and Lyu Wenfu under the already terminated patent license contract, was erroneous in both fact-finding and application of law. Pursuant to Article 184 and Article 153, Paragraph 1, Items (2) and (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court ruled: 1. The Civil Judgment (1997) Hei Jing Zhong Zi No. 68 was reversed; 2. The Civil Judgment (1994) Ha Jing San Chu Zi No. 23 of the Harbin Intermediate People's Court was affirmed. The court acceptance fees and appraisal fees for the first and second instances shall be borne by Wang Xinghua et al.

Wang Xinghua, Wang Zhenzhong, Lyu Wenfu, and Mei Mingyu, dissatisfied with the Civil Judgment (2002) Hei Gao Jian Shang Zai Zi No. 12 of the Heilongjiang High People's Court, applied to this Court for retrial. Their main grounds were: The retrial judgment seriously violated legal procedures by failing to inform the parties of the members of the collegial panel, failing to hold a hearing, and using appraisal materials without the appraiser's signature or examination of the appraiser as evidence for the judgment; and the finding that the "Termination Agreement" was valid was erroneous.

Re-respondent Radio Factory No. 1 argued in its defense: At the time of signing the patent exploitation license contract on November 1, 1990, and the termination agreement on March 20, 1991, Wang Xinghua was the right holder as recorded on the patent certificate. Although the preamble of the patent exploitation license contract stated "Wang Xinghua and two other patent designers (hereinafter referred to as Party A)," there was no power of attorney from Mei Mingyu or Wang Zhenzhong authorizing the patent license, and only Wang Xinghua signed. Both the patent license contract and the termination agreement were legally valid under the circumstances. Radio Factory No. 1 had paid patent royalties in accordance with the contract. The retrial judgment's treatment of the appraisal issue was also legally valid; the S-400A and S-400B bath boxes produced by Radio Factory No. 1 did not fall within the protection scope of Wang Xinghua's patent and had no legal rights or obligations in relation to Wang Xinghua's patent. Radio Factory No. 1 did not provide a defense opinion on the procedural issues raised in the retrial.

This Court further found: After the second-instance judgment, Radio Factory No. 1 paid Wang Xinghua et al. a portion of the patent royalties in the amount of RMB 247,609.

This Court holds that the issues in dispute in this case are: whether the "Termination Agreement" signed by Wang Xinghua is valid; and whether Radio Factory No. 1 is required to pay Wang Xinghua et al. patent license royalties.

(A) Regarding the validity of the "Termination Agreement"

Where a patentee and other non-patentee parties jointly act as one party to a patent implementation license contract, particularly where the contract also stipulates rights and obligations for such other non-patentee parties, the exercise of patent rights by the patentee shall be subject to the constraints of the contract. Without the consent of the other non-patentee parties, the patentee has no right unilaterally to terminate the patent implementation license contract that has been signed; otherwise, the legitimate rights and interests of the other parties to the contract would be prejudiced. On November 1, 1990, when the patent implementation license contract was signed, Wang Xinghua signed as the representative of Party A (Wang Xinghua, Wang Zhenzhong, and Mei Mingyu). Although the contract did not stipulate that the right to dispose of the patent was jointly owned by the three aforementioned individuals, it did provide that Party A had the right to receive the initial fee and the patent royalties. Although the contract did not specify the amount of proceeds to be received by the other two individuals, what was not specified was merely the specific allocation ratio; it was not that the two individuals were not entitled to receive proceeds. On March 20, 1991, when Wang Xinghua signed the termination agreement with Radio Factory No. 1, without the consent or authorization of the other licensors, he unilaterally terminated the previously signed patent implementation license contract, thereby harming the interests of the other licensors.

According to the facts found upon retrial, Wang Xinghua entered into the termination agreement with Radio Factory No. 1 with the intention of sidelining Wang Zhenzhong and others. Radio Factory No. 1 was fully aware of Wang Xinghua's intent and the patent ownership dispute between Wang Xinghua and Wang Zhenzhong and others. Furthermore, the termination agreement stated that the structural form of the portable individual bathtub involved in the patent implementation license contract could not be implemented in production, which was inconsistent with the facts.

Accordingly, this Court holds that the judgment upon retrial erred in finding that: (1) although Wang Xinghua signed the patent implementation license contract on behalf of Wang Zhenzhong and Mei Mingyu, the contract did not stipulate that the right to dispose of the patent was jointly owned by the three, nor did it specify the amount of proceeds for the other two; (2) as the sole patentee at the time, Wang Xinghua had the right to sign the termination agreement; and (3) Wang Xinghua and others failed to provide evidence proving Radio Factory No. 1 acted in bad faith. Based on these grounds, the retrial court incorrectly concluded that Wang Xinghua's actions complied with the provisions of the Patent Law and that the termination agreement was valid. This finding should be corrected. Radio Factory No. 1's argument that the termination agreement was valid and that it had fulfilled its obligations under the contract is not supported and is rejected.

(2) Whether Radio Factory No. 1 is required to pay patent royalties to Wang Xinghua and others

This case is a dispute over a patent implementation license contract. According to Article 5 of the patent implementation license contract signed by both parties: During the term of the contract, if required by process or other production needs, either Party A or Party B may make technical improvements to the patent, provided that such improvements do not alter the essential attributes of the patent or affect the execution of this contract. Radio Factory No. 1 shall pay the patent implementation license fees to Wang Xinghua, Wang Zhenzhong, and Mei Mingyu as agreed. As one of the patentees, Lü Wenfu is entitled to receive a corresponding share.

In the retrial judgment, having found the termination agreement valid, the court, based on expert conclusions, determined whether the two types of products manufactured by Radio Factory No. 1 fell within the scope of patent protection of Wang Xinghua and others. This exceeded the scope of trial in this case. Regardless of whether Radio Factory No. 1 continued to use the patented technology of Wang Xinghua and others, its own improved technology, or a separately patented technology, this involves a determination of patent infringement, which this Court should not adjudicate in this case.

During the retrial, the Heilongjiang High People's Court adopted an expert opinion commissioned by the court of second instance from the Intellectual Property Affairs Center of the State Science and Technology Commission, regarding whether the technical solutions of Radio Factory No. 1's S-400A type product and S-400B type patented product fell within the scope of patent protection of Wang Xinghua and others. Based on the conclusion of this expert opinion that neither type of product manufactured by Radio Factory No. 1 fell within the scope of Wang Xinghua and others' patent protection, the retrial court found that Radio Factory No. 1 was not required to pay patent royalties to Wang Xinghua and others, and that the factual findings and application of law in the judgment of second instance were erroneous. Since the aforementioned expert opinion was not presented in court and was not subject to cross-examination by the parties, the retrial court's reliance on it as the basis for its decision violates Article 66 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 47 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Procedures, thus violating statutory procedures. Radio Factory No. 1's argument that the expert opinion is legally valid, that its S-400A and S-400B bathtub products do not fall within the scope of Wang Xinghua's patent protection, and therefore there is no legal rights or obligations relationship with Wang Xinghua's patent, is not supported by this Court and is rejected.

In summary, this Court holds that the judgment upon retrial violated statutory procedures and misapplied the law, and should be corrected. The main grounds for the retrial applications of Wang Xinghua, Wang Zhenzhong, Mei Mingyu, and Lü Wenfu are established, and this Court supports them. Pursuant to Article 21, paragraph 1, item (3) of the Technology Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 12 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 153, items (2) and (4) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. The Civil Judgment (2002) Hei Gao Jian Shang Zai Zi No. 12 of the Heilongjiang High People's Court is hereby reversed;

2. Items (1) and (2) of the Civil Judgment (1997) Hei Jing Zhong Zi No. 68 of the Heilongjiang High People's Court are affirmed, namely: (1) The Civil Judgment (1993) Ha Jing San Chu Zi No. 23 of the Harbin Intermediate People's Court is reversed; (2) Heilongjiang Radio Factory No. 1 shall pay Wang Xinghua, Wang Zhenzhong, Mei Mingyu, and Lü Wenfu patent royalties in the amount of RMB 3,242,844.52. Any patent royalties previously executed shall be deducted.

The total case acceptance fees and expert evaluation fees for the first and second instances, amounting to RMB 46,224.22, shall be borne by Heilongjiang Radio Factory No. 1.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Wang Yongchang

Acting Judge: Xia Junli

Acting Judge: Wang Yanfang

November 12, 2006

Clerk: Bao Shuo

[Profile of the Presiding Judge]

Wang Yongchang, Senior Judge: Born in 1956, Master of Laws, appointed as a judge of the Supreme People's Court in 2001.
